lessons.title: Crypto and Virtual Digital Assets: Why the 30% Rule Is Different

body.text: Crypto sits outside the capital gains system you have learned so far. There is no short-term or long-term, no deduction except cost, and a loss on one coin cannot reduce tax on a gain on another. It is the harshest tax treatment of any asset class in this course.

children.text: Rohan, a 26-year-old graphic designer in Indore, traded crypto on an Indian exchange through tax year 2026-27. He made ₹1,20,000 on Bitcoin and ₹30,000 on Ether, but lost ₹80,000 on Solana. He expected to pay tax on his net profit of ₹70,000. His actual taxable income from crypto was ₹1,50,000.
What Counts as a Virtual Digital Asset

markDefs.definition: Broadly, any information, code, number or token generated through cryptographic or similar means that provides a digital representation of value, including cryptocurrencies and NFTs, but excluding Indian and foreign currency. Defined in section 2(47A) of the 1961 Act.

children.text: , a category defined in section 2(47A) of the 1961 Act, carried into the 2025 Act. It covers cryptocurrencies, stablecoins and most tokens, as well as non-fungible tokens (NFTs). Indian and foreign currency, including the RBI's digital rupee, are excluded, and the government has notified a few exclusions such as gift cards and reward points.

children.text: Under the special 30% rule (section 115BBH of the 1961 Act, carried into the 2025 Act), each profitable VDA transfer is taxed on its own at 30%. Losses on other transfers are simply ignored. The tax department's position, reflected in the ITR schedules, is that a loss on one token cannot be set off even against a gain on a different token.

cells: Ignored: no set-off, no carry forward

body.title: Rohan's Crypto Tax
body.prompt: Rohan has gains of ₹1,20,000 on Bitcoin and ₹30,000 on Ether, and a loss of ₹80,000 on Solana. What is his tax on VDA income at 30%, before cess, in rupees?
body.explanation: The Solana loss is ignored. Taxable VDA income = ₹1,20,000 + ₹30,000 = ₹1,50,000. Tax = 30% of ₹1,50,000 = ₹45,000. Add 4% cess for ₹46,800.

body.label: What the Loss Rule Cost Rohan
body.context: If the ₹80,000 Solana loss could be set off, tax would be 30% of ₹70,000 = ₹21,000. Instead he pays ₹45,000 before cess, ₹24,000 more.

body.title: What Can You Deduct?
body.question: Rohan bought Ether for ₹2,00,000, paid ₹1,500 in exchange trading fees and GST, and sold it for ₹2,30,000. What is his taxable VDA income on this trade?
options: ₹0, because fees wipe out the gain
body.explanation: Only the cost of acquisition can be deducted from VDA sale value. Exchange fees and GST on them are not allowed. Taxable income = ₹2,30,000 − ₹2,00,000 = ₹30,000, taxed at 30%.

children.text: 1% TDS on the Sale Value, Not the Profit

Under section 194S of the 1961 Act, carried into the 2025 Act, 1% TDS is deducted on the consideration for a VDA transfer. For most individuals, it applies once transfers cross ₹50,000 in a financial year; for others, the threshold is ₹10,000. On Indian exchanges, the exchange deducts it automatically. If Rohan sold ₹12,00,000 of crypto during the year, ₹12,000 would be deducted even if his trades made a loss overall.

body.title: TDS on What?
body.textWithBlank: The 1% TDS on crypto is deducted on the ___ of each transfer, not on your profit.
body.explanation: TDS applies to the total consideration. It shows up in your AIS and Form 26AS and is credited against your final tax. If your total tax is lower than the TDS deducted, you claim the difference as a refund in your ITR.

body.title: How India's Crypto Tax Rules Took Shape

events.title: 30% tax on VDA income
events.description: Flat 30% tax introduced with no deduction except cost and no loss set-off.

events.title: 1% TDS on transfers
events.description: TDS on VDA transfer consideration began, tracking trades through exchanges and buyers.

events.title: Crypto brought under anti-money laundering law
events.description: VDA service providers became reporting entities under PMLA, and offshore exchanges serving Indians were later required to register with FIU-IND.

events.title: Income-tax Act, 2025 and tighter reporting
events.description: The 30% tax and 1% TDS carried over unchanged. Budget 2026 added penalties for crypto service providers that fail to report VDA transactions.

body.title: Neha's Staking Rewards
body.scenario: Neha stakes Ether on an exchange and receives staking rewards worth ₹20,000 on the days they are credited. Four months later she sells those reward tokens for ₹26,000.
body.prompt: How are the rewards taxed when received, and how is the later sale taxed?
body.modelAnswer: When credited, the rewards are generally treated as income from other sources at their fair market value, so ₹20,000 is added to her income and taxed at slab rate. On sale, the transfer is a VDA transfer taxed at 30%. The value already taxed on receipt is commonly treated as her cost, so taxable VDA income is ₹26,000 − ₹20,000 = ₹6,000, and tax is ₹1,800 before cess. The treatment of staking, mining and airdrops is less settled than trading, so keep screenshots of the value on the credit date and take advice for large amounts.

body.title: Deep Dive: Swaps, Payments, Gifts and Offshore Exchanges

children.text: Crypto-to-crypto swaps: exchanging Bitcoin for Ether is a transfer of Bitcoin. Any gain on the Bitcoin is taxable at 30%, and TDS can apply to both legs of the trade.
Paying with crypto: using crypto to buy goods or services is a transfer of the crypto at its value on that date, even though you never converted it to rupees.

Gifts: gifting crypto is not a transfer by the giver for this purpose, but the receiver may be taxed on its value as income from other sources if it exceeds ₹50,000 in a year and does not come from a relative or fall within another exemption. The receiver's cost for a later sale is generally the value taxed at receipt.

Offshore exchanges: if you trade on an exchange that does not deduct Indian TDS, the obligation to deduct can fall on the buyer in peer-to-peer trades, and you must still report every trade in your ITR.

body.text: Every VDA transfer must be reported trade by trade in Schedule VDA of your ITR, with dates of acquisition and transfer, cost and sale value. Exchanges report TDS against your PAN, so it appears in your AIS. A mismatch between what exchanges report and what you file is a common trigger for tax notices.

cards.definition: Crypto, stablecoins, most tokens and NFTs. Excludes Indian and foreign currency and notified items.
Flat rate on each gain, regardless of holding period, plus surcharge and cess.
The only deduction allowed against VDA sale value. Fees and GST are not deductible.
VDA losses cannot reduce other VDA gains or any other income, and cannot be carried forward.
Deducted on sale value of VDA transfers above ₹50,000 a year for most individuals.
The ITR schedule where every crypto transfer is reported with dates, cost and sale value.

body.title: Crypto Tax Hygiene for the Year
steps: Download the full trade history and TDS report from every exchange and wallet you use
Compute gain or loss for each transfer separately, using cost of acquisition only
Add up only the gains for taxable VDA income, and ignore losses
Record the value of staking rewards, airdrops and received gifts on the date received
Match TDS shown in your AIS against the exchange reports before filing
File ITR-2 or ITR-3 and complete Schedule VDA trade by trade

points: Crypto and NFTs are virtual digital assets, taxed at a flat 30% regardless of holding period
Only the cost of acquisition can be deducted; exchange fees and GST cannot
A loss on one VDA cannot be set off against a gain on another VDA or any other income, and cannot be carried forward
1% TDS is deducted on the sale value, not profit, and is credited against your final tax
Swaps, crypto payments and staking rewards can all create taxable events
Every VDA transfer must be reported in Schedule VDA, and exchanges report your trades against your PAN

body.text: This lesson is for educational purposes only and is not tax or investment advice. Crypto assets are highly volatile and are not regulated by SEBI or RBI as investments. Figures are illustrative. Tax rules for VDAs reflect the Income-tax Act, 2025 as amended by the Finance Act, 2026, for tax year 2026-27, and some areas such as staking remain unsettled. Consult a qualified tax professional before acting.
